newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish jobless to fall to 13.5 pct 1998 -ministry.
newsitem.headline: Finnish jobless to fall to 13.5 pct 1998 -ministry.

text.p: Finnish employment will improve at a quicker pace in 1997 and 1998 than in the past few years as economic growth is spreading to labour-intensive sectors like construction and services, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.
Brisk growth -- forecast by the ministry at 4.6 percent this year -- would increase demand for labour "by 40,000 jobs," the ministry's economics department said in a new forecast.
It added that labour supply would rise only marginally.
"The number of unemployed will probably fall by 34,000 this year. The average unemployment rate for the full year will fall below 15 percent," the ministry said. @
It said there would be a "stronger downward trend in unemployment". In 1996, the jobless rate was 16.3 percent, down from 17.2 percent in 1995.
"Recovery will be especially apparent in construction although industrial building is declining, commercial construction and home building are clearly on the rise," the ministry said.
"Demand for services will also increase," it said. @
Next year, economic growth would begin to provide jobs "at a faster pace than in recent years, with, above all, labour-intensive sectors such as building and services expanding," it said.
The average unemployment rate for 1998 "should fall close to 13.5 percent," it said.
The five-party left-right-green government's official target is to halve the 1995 jobless rate to about eight to nine percent by the end of its term in 1999.
